Animation

  • Animation in CSS means making an element move or change automatically over time. It helps make a website look more attractive and interactive.
  • CSS animation works in a similar way—it changes an element from one state to another automatically.
  • CSS Animation is a feature that allows HTML elements to change their style (such as position, size, color, rotation, or opacity) over a specified period of time without using JavaScript.

In CSS, there are 2 main types of animations:

  1. Transition
  2. Animation (@keyframes)

1. Transition

  • Changes an element from one state to another.
  • It starts only when an event happens, such as hovering (:hover), clicking, or focusing.
  • Used for simple effects.

CSS Animation + Keyframes

selector { animation-name: animationName;
animation-duration: 2s;
animation-iteration-count: infinite;
animation-timing-function: ease;
animation-delay: 1s;
animation-direction: normal;
}

@keyframes animation-name {
0% {
/* Starting styles */
} 50% {
/* Middle styles */
} 100% {
/* Ending styles */
} }
